mainEntity.name: How does intended building use dictate interior finish-out decisions?

acceptedAnswer.text: Whether a space is classified as residential, commercial office, or industrial workshop dictates entirely different code requirements for fire separation, ventilation, and energy performance. If you change a metal building previously used for ag storage or warehousing into conditioned retail or office space, local codes often mandate upgraded fire-rated drywall partitions, minimum restroom fixture counts, and stricter accessibility access under ADA guidelines. Defining this early prevents expensive design adjustments mid-construction when local plan reviewers review your finish-out drawings.
acceptedAnswer.description: Intended occupancy determines mandatory fire-separation ratings, ADA accessibility compliance, restroom requirements, and HVAC ventilation standards under local building codes.
